# Setting Up: Turning the Question Into Symbols

<!-- STEP id="whats-already-known" -->
An object starts moving at velocity **u**. It speeds up steadily — constant acceleration **a** — for a time **t**. By the end, its velocity is **v**.

That's exactly the straight-line velocity-time graph from the last lesson: starting height u, ending height v, running for t seconds.

<!-- STEP id="two-open-questions" -->
Two things we don't have a direct formula for yet:

1. What is **v**, in terms of u, a and t — without drawing a graph every time?
2. How far did the object actually travel — the displacement **s** — during that time?

<!-- STEP id="the-one-tool-we-have" -->
We already have one exact tool: the definition of acceleration itself.

$$a = \frac{v - u}{t}$$

Everything in this lesson comes from squeezing that one definition, and one picture, as hard as they'll go.
